status: RENDERED LOCALLY, NOT UPLOADED. This plan is the second 2026-10-06 take, rendered at a85056b and recorded again at f7512bf, cut after the judge review of the take at 81d6144. Its content opens on Android TV emulator footage from CI run 37475795991: the debug APK built at f423ba5 on an AOSP Android TV emulator, Android 14 / API 34, loading the public demo (build ea2cff5, record-only). The footage plays from 8.88 s, the board as it first shows, at 1x, with two holds of a static frame; the home screen and the black cold start before it are not shown, because CI launched the app by intent, not with a D-pad press on a tile. That is footage, not a Fire TV device and not a runtime receipt; the Android TV emulator runtime receipt is a separate file, android_tv_runtime_receipt.json. The rest is a local run of this repository in desktop Chromium at 1920x1080 CSS (the desktop layout, not the Fire TV WebView's 960x540 CSS) with MERCURY_OFFLINE=1, driven through the D-pad bridge the Leanback app calls. A label under each picture names its source. An emulator beat's seconds are its footage window plus its holds; a desktop beat's seconds are its measured hold, the length of its synthesized audio plus a 0.65 s tail, from video/generate-narration.py. The media lives outside the repository; video/README.md says where. The event FAQ permits the Android TV Emulator and does not require physical hardware.

beats.narration_text: On an Android TV emulator, the public demo asks on its own: checkout A P I, twelve point nine times baseline.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage from 8.88 s of journey.mp4 at 1x: the board as it first shows (frame 19, 8.856 s), Not asked; CHECKING at 10.074 s (frame 21), checkout-api ASKING at 10.428 s (frame 23), checkout-api 12.9x, TEMPORAL CANDIDATE, Commit 4f1c2ab from the demo's invented deploy feed at 11.160 s (frame 24), all five rows at 11.630 s (frame 28). That static board is held at 12.00 s. The home screen and the black cold start before 8.856 s are not shown.

beats.narration_text: Right, then center. A rollback is staged, and its lease counts down.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage from 14.40 s: D-pad Right moves focus to Stage rollback at 14.439 s (frame 29), Center at 15.296 s (frame 30), ROLLBACK STAGED with a 300 s lease at 15.847 s (frame 31), counting down to 296 s.

beats.narration_text: Right, then center confirms. Recorded, no pipeline contacted: this demo is record only.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage from 20.28 s: focus on Confirm since 20.110 s (frame 37), Center at 21.250 s (frame 39), RECORDED, no pipeline contacted at 21.691 s (frame 40), static on the board until 26.290 s.

beats.narration_text: Center publishes the handoff: shared revision thirteen.
beats.visual_action: Emulator footage from 26.20 s to the end: Center scrolls to the handoff with focus on Publish handoff at 26.290 s (frame 42), the shared handoff, SHARED REVISION 13, HTTP 200 at 26.588 s (frame 43). The last frame is held 2.52 s.

beats.narration_text: The rest is the same board in a desktop browser, run locally from this commit. It has its own fixtures, so the commits differ, and its handoff starts again at revision one. Mercury names a commit only when exactly one runtime change landed before the spike.
beats.visual_action: The desktop take begins: the loaded board in desktop Chromium at 1920x1080 CSS (the desktop layout, not the Fire TV WebView's 960x540), focus on Ask what changed, and the desktop label under the picture. No key pressed.

beats.narration_text: It answered on load, before any key was pressed. Four of the five rows name no commit. A refusal never calls the deploy innocent.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the board. The five rows read Temporal candidate (with a commit), Nothing to revert, Cannot attribute, Cannot attribute and Insufficient data, each from the server's answer.

beats.narration_text: Down walks the rows. Release train shows a spike well above its baseline, but several runtime changes landed in the window before it, and no metric says which one did it. Mercury cannot attribute this, and offers no rollback. Rolling back would be a guess.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Down four times to release-train, then Center, all before the second caption. The verdict reads Cannot attribute this with the number of changes that landed, Next reads No rollback offered, and Stage rollback and Confirm are disabled.

beats.narration_text: Up, up, up, center. On checkout A P I, exactly one runtime change landed before the spike, so Mercury names it, and prints its own odds: on held-out generated cases a named commit is the cause fifty percent of the time, if a fault shows within seventy five minutes.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Up three times to checkout-api and Center, each on its spoken word, before the caption that names checkout-api. The verdict names the commit as the only runtime change, quotes its message, and reads 50.0% held-out precision (synthetic, ≤75m lag).

beats.narration_text: On this board, the reading and the commit each carry a stamp. The metric is an offline fixture, generated locally. The commit is one of Mercury's own, standing in for a deploy feed.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the OFFLINE FIXTURE stamp under the reading and the dashed STAND-IN stamp against Mercury's commits. No key pressed. (The public demo in the emulator footage names records from an invented fixture feed instead; the label under the footage says so.)

beats.narration_text: Up, right, center: the rollback is staged. Right, center confirms it, and the board holds recorded, not sent. Center publishes the handoff. Down shows the evidence behind the odds: fifty eight namings, in eleven hundred sixty synthetic cases.
beats.visual_action: Each press on its spoken word. Up, Right to Stage rollback, Center: Rollback staged. Right to Confirm, Center: nothing scrolls, the large figure reads RECORDED, no pipeline contacted, and the legend reads Next press: Publish responder handoff. Center publishes: HTTP 200, the handoff's responder, facts and next step clear the key bar under the rollback steps. Down lands on Incident evidence: 50.0% over 58 namings in 1160 synthetic labelled cases.

beats.narration_text: The ring jumps to the nearest control in the direction pressed, and the label at the bottom right names it. Center opens delivery velocity, and Back now reads: back to the wall.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Right to Delivery velocity, Center. The panel opens and the BACK legend changes from Exit to the Fire TV launcher to Back to the wall.

beats.narration_text: Its answer is a recording, stamped offline fixture, because no GitHub token is set. Back returns to the wall, not out of the app. Cloud spend is a fixture too, marked synthetic.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Down scrolls the rest of the DORA answer into view with its OFFLINE FIXTURE stamp; the cursor stays in the panel. Back returns to the wall and the legend changes back. Right to Cloud spend and Center before the third caption: the spend answer carries OFFLINE FIXTURE and says its figures are SYNTHETIC. Back to the wall.

beats.narration_text: Down, down, center: the server reports its build, the commit on the opening card, in fixture mode. The emulator footage came from C I, not a Fire TV device.
beats.visual_action: Down to How it answers, Down to Check, Center, each on its spoken word. The connection line reads GET /health returned 200, the build's short SHA, and GitHub live: no, fixture mode.
